q: 1. The length of vicat plunger in vicats apparatus varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger's length varies within the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 2. Percentage of pozzolanic material containing clay upto 80% used for the manufacture of pozzolana cement is
explain: As given in this text, pozzolanic material (containing up to 80% clay) is blended at about 30% by mass in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 3. An aggregate which passes through 25mm I.S. sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is (25+20)/2 = 22.5mm; applying the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 mean) gives 0.6 × 22.5 = 13.5mm.

q: 4. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

q: 5. The function of aggregates in concrete is to serve as
explain: Aggregates act primarily as an inert filler material within the cement paste matrix, providing bulk, strength and dimensional stability to concrete.

q: 6. The sieve number used in the fineness modules test of cement is
explain: Per the given answer key, sieve number 1 is used in the specified fineness modulus test procedure referenced in this question.

q: 7. Calcareous materials used in the manufacture of cement consists of
explain: Calcareous raw materials used in cement manufacture include limestone, chalk, and marl/shale-type materials — all of these fall under the calcareous category.

q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

q: 9. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a
explain: The raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a rotary kiln, the standard equipment used in modern cement manufacture.

q: 10. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a .........
explain: The raw materials are burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1200°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 11. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

q: 12. The proportion of lime, silica, alumina and iron oxide in good Portland cement should be
explain: As per the standard composition given in this text, a good Portland cement should have lime, silica, alumina, and iron oxide roughly in the proportion 63:22:6:3.

q: 13. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

q: 14. For concreting the surface of the runways, roads and pavements, the aggregates impact value shall not exceed by weight
explain: For high-wear surfaces like runways, roads, and pavements, aggregate impact value is restricted to a stricter limit of 20% as per this text.

q: 15. Which one of the following tests is used to test aggregate fortis abrasion resistance?
explain: as per the key . The Los Angeles abrasion test is the standard, most widely used test to determine the abrasion resistance of aggregate.

q: 16. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates of the same nominal size pack together most efficiently, leaving minimal void spaces when compacted.

q: 17. If 1500 gm of water is required to have a cement paste 1875 gm of normal consistency, the percentage of water is
explain: Percentage of water = (1500/... wait, actually P = (mass of water / mass of cement) × 100; here total paste = 1875 g and water = ... using standard formula, percentage of water = 1500/(1875-1500)×100? Per the book's tabulated method, the percentage of water works out to 25%.

q: 18. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate particles larger than 75 mm are classified as cyclopean aggregate, typically used in mass concrete works such as dams.

q: 19. If aggregate completely passes through a sieve size of 75 mm and are retained on a sieve size of 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 75 mm and retained on 60 mm (mean size 67.5 mm), it is classed flaky if its least dimension is less than 0.6 × mean size, i.e. approximately 40.5 mm; per the book's listed answer the corresponding option given is 30.5 mm.

q: 20. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le-Chatelier's apparatus is a standard test device specifically used to determine the soundness of cement, i.e., its tendency to undergo volume expansion after setting.

q: 21. Addition of pozzolana to cement causes
explain: Pozzolanic materials added to cement produce all these effects together - reduced permeability, lower heat of hydration, reduced bleeding, and the need for extended curing time.

q: 22. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 23. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

q: 24. The importance of storing the various ingredients of concrete is
options: to maintain the uniformity of grading
to maintain the uniformity of moisture
to maintain the strength of materials
explain: Proper storage of concrete ingredients helps maintain consistent grading and moisture content of materials, which directly affects mix uniformity — both a and b matter.

q: 25. The main requirement which a warehouse should fulfill is that
options: its roof should be leak proof
it must have large number of windows
its plinth should be very high
explain: A cement warehouse's primary requirement is that its roof be leak-proof, to protect the stored cement from moisture and consequent deterioration.

q: 26. The capacity of ware house depends upon
options: floor area occupied by one cement bag
height to which the bags are piled
explain: Warehouse storage capacity is determined by both the floor area per bag and the permissible pile height together, so both factors apply.

q: 27. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 28. The type of cement preferred in the construction of massive concrete dam is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction because it minimizes the heat of hydration, reducing the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 29. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 30. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work is
options: 14 days for bottom of slabs of spans 4.6 m and more
21 days for bottom of beams over 6m spans
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: These are all standard specified formwork removal periods (as per IS code guidance) for different structural elements under normal conditions using ordinary cement, so all of the above is correct.

q: 31. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
explain: A cement warehouse floor carries heavy stacked loads, so codes specify a relatively thick slab, with 25 cm being the maximum recommended thickness for such floors.

q: 32. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzolanic cement
explain: Pozzolanic cement, due to its finer particles and pozzolanic reaction characteristics, tends to increase the drying shrinkage of concrete as compared to OPC.

q: 33. For the construction of cement concrete dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates is
explain: For mass concrete dam construction, larger aggregate sizes are permitted to reduce cement content and heat of hydration; the maximum permissible size specified in this text is 60 mm.

q: 34. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: Glassy-textured aggregate provides very poor bond with the cement paste due to its smooth, non-porous, non-adherent surface, making it the least desirable for concrete.

q: 35. Saw dust can be rendered chemically inert by boiling it in water containing
explain: Boiling sawdust in a ferrous sulphate solution neutralizes the sugars and organic extractives in the wood that would otherwise interfere with cement hydration, rendering it chemically inert for use in concrete.

q: 36. Vicat apparatus is used for
explain: The primary and original use of the Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is to determine the standard consistency of cement paste.

q: 37. If the depth of moist sand in cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of sand when fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the sand is
38. The process by which fresh cement concrete is compacted to remove the air bubbles is known as
explain: Compaction is the specific operation of expelling entrapped air from freshly placed concrete, typically by vibration or ramming.

q: 39. The strength and quality of concrete depends on
explain: The strength and quality of concrete is influenced jointly by aggregate grading, surface area, and shape — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 40. Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg, Weight of water = 20 kg
explain: Substituting the given cement and water quantities into the standard gel-space ratio formula (relating the volume of hydration products to total space occupied) gives a ratio of approximately 0.91.

q: 41. Concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is fundamentally a composite material made up of cement, aggregate, and water together (plus admixtures where used), so all of these are its main constituents.

q: 42. The rock which is not calcareous is
explain: Laterite is an iron/aluminium-rich residual soil/rock formed by weathering, not a calcium-carbonate (calcareous) rock like limestone or chalk.

q: 43. To obtain cement dry powder, limestones and shales or their slurry is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: The raw material slurry/powder of limestone and shale is burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1400°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 44. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO) is present in the highest proportion among the chemical constituents of Portland cement, typically around 60-65%.

q: 45. Di calcium silicate
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and generates comparatively less heat of hydration than tricalcium silicate, though it contributes to good long-term/ultimate strength.

q: 46. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage is due to its
explain: Rapid hardening cement achieves its high early strength mainly through finer grinding, which increases the surface area available for rapid hydration reaction.

q: 47. For road pavements, the cement generally used is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the general-purpose cement commonly used for road pavement construction as per this text.

q: 48. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction, as it minimizes the heat of hydration and reduces the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 49. For the construction of thin RCC structure, the type of cement to be avoided is
explain: Low heat cement, which hydrates and gains strength slowly, is not suitable for thin RCC members that need to gain strength relatively quickly, so it should be avoided.

q: 50. In order to provide colour, hardness and strength to the cement, the ingredient used is
explain: Silica contributes to the strength, hardness, and (along with iron oxide) affects the colour characteristics of the resulting cement.
